The diagram shows the velocity-time graph of two moving cars P and Q. The graph indicates that

(Velocity (m s⁻¹) vs time (s): car P rises linearly from 0 to 50 m/s by t = 10 s, then stays constant at 50 m/s up to time t, after which its velocity curves up to a peak near t = 45 s and then falls to zero at t = 70 s. Car Q rises linearly from 0 to a higher constant velocity, reaching it at time t, then stays constant until t = 70 s.)

options.label: A
options.text: After 20 s, P is behind Q

options.label: B
options.text: Car Q is moving with a constant acceleration from 0 to 60 seconds

options.label: C
options.text: Acceleration of the car Q is not zero at any point during the whole journey

options.label: D
options.text: The velocity of car P is increasing at a decreasing rate

stem: A parachutist jumps off a plane and opens the parachute at time \(t_1\). He eventually reaches a steady speed and finally hits the floor at time \(t_2\). Which of the following speed-time graphs best shows the parachutist's descent?

options.label: A
options.text: Speed rises to a peak at \(t_1\), then decreases gradually and levels off to a constant (terminal) speed until \(t_2\)

options.label: B
options.text: Speed starts at a maximum at t = 0 and decreases steadily to zero at \(t_2\)

options.label: C
options.text: Speed starts at a maximum, stays high until \(t_1\), then drops sharply to a low constant value until \(t_2\)

options.label: D
options.text: Speed rises linearly to a peak at \(t_1\), then drops almost instantly to a low constant value until \(t_2\)

stem:
A train moves from one station to another in two hours' time. Its speed-time graph during the motion is shown in the figure. Identify the correct statement(s) regarding this graph.

(Speed (km h⁻¹) vs time (h): speed rises from 0 to 20 km/h during 0 to 0.50 h, stays constant at 20 km/h from 0.50 to 0.75 h, rises to 50 km/h at 1.00 h (point C), then falls steadily to 0 at 2.00 h.)

1. The maximum acceleration during the journey is 120 km/h².
2. The distance covered during the time interval from 0.75 to 1 hr is 8.75 km.
3. During the time interval from 0 to 0.5 hrs, the train moves with constant acceleration.

options.label: A
options.text: Only (i) is correct

options.label: B
options.text: All (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct

options.label: C
options.text: Only (ii) is correct

options.label: D
options.text: Both (i) and (iii) are correct

stem:
What would you conclude about the variation in the velocity of a cyclist from the given graph?

(The graph has acceleration a on the y-axis and time t on the x-axis. Acceleration increases linearly with time — a straight line from the origin O up to point P, with R marked on the time axis directly below P.)

options.label: A
options.text: Velocity changes linearly if acceleration is changing non-linearly

options.label: B
options.text: Velocity changes non-linearly if acceleration is changing linearly

options.label: C
options.text: Velocity becomes uniform if acceleration becomes infinite

options.label: D
options.text: Velocity becomes zero if acceleration becomes zero

A dancer is demonstrating dance steps along a straight line. The position-time graph of the dancer is given here. The average velocity of the dancer during the time interval t = 2 s to t = 9 s is

(Position x (m) vs time t (s): x rises from 0 to 2 m by t = 2 s (A), stays at 2 m to t = 3 s (B), rises to 4 m at t = 4.5 s (C), falls to 0 at t = 6 s (D), falls to −2 m at t = 7 s (E), stays at −2 m to t = 8 s (F), then rises to 0 at t = 9 s (G).)
